text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool 'eu-west-2a' saturated · available_gpus=0 · queue_len=12,400 · autoscaler_state=ScaleLimitHit · affected_pools: gpupool-eu-west-2a · links: https://console.internal/redwood/alerts/5237102468 :rotating_light:
ashwin: ack — I'm oncall for infra, jumping in. @leah @daniel please +1 if you can join, looks like autoscaler didn't scale past configured limit and queue is growing fast.
leah: on it. seeing a spike of long-running tiny jobs, many from the rerank service. 429s in prod metrics and client 503s.
daniel: paging infra now. autoscaler logs show repeated `scaleUp failed: providerQuotaExceeded` followed by `scaleLimitReached` at the operator level. snip of logs:```ERROR autoscaler/controller.go:724 scaleUp failed: ScaleLimitReached current=48 max=48 request=4```
sara: Support here. We're seeing escalations from 3 customers in EU complaining about timeouts; two are on dedicated contracts. CS has opened tickets  RED-3287, RED-3290.
mike: infra - I'm looking at provider quotas, EU region's soft limit is at 48 GPUs which matches the max. There's some idle reserved capacity marked for internal CI that we can evict as emergency.
ashwin: agree with eviction as immediate mitigation. Steps: 1) reduce low-priority pools 2) temporarily bump operator max if cloud quota allows 3) enable fallback routing to a lower-cost model variant for affected routes. Any objections?
leah: no objections. I'll start evicting CI workloads from gpupool-eu-west-2a. Command I ran:```gcloud compute instances delete --zone eu-west-2a ci-runner-09 --project redwood-ci --quiet``` will drain two nodes in ~90s.
daniel: I'll open a provider request to increase GPU quota, but that can take hours. For immediate relief I can toggle the autoscaler override to allow burst up to 56 if the provider grant shows available quota.
mike: quick note — evicting will free up ~6 GPUs. also we can enable model-fallback routing in the router service:```PATCH /v1/routes/serve-config { "fallback_model": "llama-7b-q4" }``` this will reduce token cost and usage per request.
sara: notifying affected customers: CS message queued. We'll offer temporary rate-limited fallback and ETA for full resolution.
ashwin: doing a coordinated handoff to oncall infra. @mike please confirm when eviction completes. I'll pause new low-priority scheduling from the scheduler UI: `scheduler.disableQueue(low-priority)`.
mike: eviction done — freed 6 GPUs. queue down from 12.4k -> 9.6k, error 503 rate decreased ~30%. dashboard: https://console.internal/redwood/dash/gpu-pools?pool=eu-west-2a
leah: autoscaler now sees capacity, attempted scale up but operator still returning ScaleLimitReached — looks like operator enforcing `max=48` from cluster annotation. I'm going to patch the annotation to max=56 for now.
daniel: patching operator:```kubectl patch gpupool gpupool-eu-west-2a -p '{"spec": {"max": 56}}' --type merge``` applied. autoscaler logs now: `scaleUp accepted, provisioning 8 nodes`
ashwin: provisioning in progress. Reminder: we also flipped fallback routing so premium endpoints are routed to cheaper model where acceptable. Sara, did CS send the update?
sara: yes sent to affected customers with conservative ETA of 2h for steady state + note about temporary degraded throughput. One customer asked for credit — I'm collecting usage impact calc.
support-bot: Incident note: Created support case RED-3291 for enterprise customer "Pine Labs" latency regressions.
mike: cloud provider returned capacity grant for 12 GPUs after manual request — nodes booting. pool will reach target in ~6 minutes.
leah: pool healthy, queue now 1.2k, 500/s token throughput back to normal for most routes. still seeing some stuck tasks in the queue from rerank jobs; will evict them if they timeout.
daniel: start a small canary rollback of rerank job config that resulted in many tiny tasks — rolling back to previous retry policy.```PATCH /api/v1/services/rerank/config {"retry": "fixed-1s","batch_size": 8}```
ashwin: good. summary so far: root cause = operator max coupled with provider quota + sudden surge of small rerank jobs; mitigation = evict CI, patch operator max, enable fallback routing, rollback rerank policy, request provider quota increase.
sara: impact summary for postmortem: ~2h partial degradation, ~3 premium customers affected, some timed-out requests for high qps routes. CS estimates ~0.08% of total calls affected during window.
leah: temporary follow-ups: 1) revert operator max change only after we confirm quota increase and autoscaler tests (owner: daniel) 2) add guard in scheduler to avoid scheduling CI in production pools (owner: mike) 3) add rejection early for tiny high-frequency jobs at ingress (owner: leah)
daniel: creating tickets: INFRA-1120 (operator max gating + audit), INFRA-1121 (quota automation with provider), RERANK-305 (retry config rollback + rate limit). I'll link in postmortem.
ashwin: postmortem owner assigned to me. I'll draft timeline and RCA. Action items: - emergency quota playbook (owner: daniel) - auto-evict low-priority CI (owner: mike) - add autoscaler metric alert for 'ScaleLimitReached' (owner: leah) - runbook update for fallback routing (owner: ashwin)
mike: noting that we should add a soft limit that prevents pushing CI into production pools; I'll propose a scheduler label enforcement PR.
sara: CS action: outreach completed, follow-up scheduled for tomorrow at 10am GMT.
ops-bot: Incident status -> RESOLVED · summary: capacity restored and autoscaler resumed normal operation · duration: ~1h 52m · postmortem: https://docs.internal/redwood/postmortems/5237102468-gpu-eviction-operator-limit
ashwin: thanks everyone. I'll post the draft postmortem in #postmortems by EOD and include the timeline + monitoring improvements. Close this thread when postmortem is up. :thumbsup:
